messages.content:
Assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category. Here are worked examples, then the case to code.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: I21

Example 3
Hospital course: A 34-year-old woman presented with fever, rigors, dysuria and right flank tenderness. Urine microscopy showed pyuria and culture grew Escherichia coli. Computed tomography showed a swollen right kidney with no abscess. She improved on intravenous ceftriaxone.
Answer: N10

Example 4
Hospital course: An 81-year-old woman was brought in after a fall at home. She could not weight-bear and the right leg was shortened and externally rotated. A pelvic radiograph showed a displaced subcapital fracture of the right femoral neck. She underwent hemiarthroplasty on day one.
Answer: S72

Example 5
Hospital course: A 19-year-old man presented with 18 hours of periumbilical pain that migrated to the right iliac fossa, with anorexia and a low-grade fever. There was guarding at McBurney's point and the white cell count was 15.2. Laparoscopy confirmed an inflamed, non-perforated appendix.
Answer: K35

Example 6
Hospital course: A 64-year-old woman with a history of oestrogen-receptor-positive breast carcinoma treated five years earlier presented with progressive thoracic back pain. Magnetic resonance imaging showed deposits in T7 and T9 with no cord compression. Biopsy confirmed deposits of breast origin and she received palliative radiotherapy to the spine.
Answer: C79

Discharge Summary:

Admission date: N/A
Discharge date: N/A

Patient Information: 
The patient is a 71-year-old Finnish male diagnosed with early onset Parkinson's disease at the age of 40.

Hospital Course:

During the years 2016-2017, the patient was categorized at stage 2.5 of the modified Hoehn and Yahr Scale, with a United Parkinson's Disease Rating Scale (UPDRS) score of 41/199. The patient demonstrated rigidity of the lower limbs, shortness of steps, and postural instability, but no tremors. He has experienced a mild gait disturbance with occasional freezing recently. The progression of his illness has been slow, with a sustained response to medication.

Diagnostic Tests:
Dopamine transporter (DaT) single-photon emission computerized tomography (SPECT) of the brain was performed and demonstrated reduced density of DA synaptic terminals in the caudate and putamen consistent with degenerative Parkinson's disease.

Medical History:
The patient has no reported family history of Parkinson's disease.

Genetic Analysis:
Targeted next-generation sequencing revealed that the patient carried a novel homozygous c.194G > A variant in exon 3 of the PARK2 gene, causing an amino acid change p.Ser65Asn (S65N) in the PARKIN protein. The variant is very rare, but the site is highly conserved in vertebrates, and in silico analysis of the variant predicted that the mutation is deleterious.
Discharge Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Follow-Up Care and Recommendations:
The patient should follow up with his healthcare provider regularly to monitor his condition and adjust medication as needed. The patient should be advised to continue engaging in regular physical activity and cognitive stimulation.

Answer with the three-character category only.

text:
The case describes early-onset Parkinson's disease with a homozygous PARK2 (parkin) variant. In ICD-10-AM, G20 is Parkinson's disease, which includes "juvenile" and "early-onset" forms. Genetic parkinsonism would still be coded to G20. The alternative would be G23 or G21, but the record describes degenerative Parkinson's disease with a sustained response to medication, so G20 fits best.

**G20**
